memory_update.text: GENK should remain a high-priority Layer 2 diligence target for this node because it combines restaurant expansion, named distributor reliance, and related-party procurement risk.
NATH is a clean small-cap supplier-concentration case tied to hot dogs and fries; it may be better mapped as branded foodservice plus restaurant procurement rather than a simple QSR operator.
Centralized purchasing organizations and sole purchasing-agent structures can convert a restaurant brand thesis into a procurement-scale thesis, as seen in DIN's CSCS disclosure.
RAVE remains weakly evidenced: verify whether third-party distributor agreements are economically material or merely standard franchisor operating infrastructure before advancing beyond Layer 1.

node: Small/mid-cap restaurant operators with supplier concentration or related-party procurement
summary: Layer 1B expands the universe around restaurant operators where procurement structure, supplier concentration, distribution agreements, or related-party vendors may matter as much as brand-level traffic. The strongest direct underfollowed lead is GENK because filings disclose both a major Sysco relationship and a related-party supplier. NATH is a cleaner small-cap procurement-concentration case around hot dogs and fries. DIN is a larger small-cap reference/underfollowed hybrid because its purchasing organization structure makes supply-chain scale a key part of the thesis. RAVE is a micro-cap speculative shadow candidate: relevant because it discloses third-party distribution arrangements, but current evidence is weaker and needs direct 10-K verification.
